children: rose 0.86% premarket after Mark Zuckerberg argued in a post on X that competition and liability give AI companies sufficient reason to act on safety individually. Those comments were seen to break from calls by other lab leaders for a coordinated slowdown. Anthropic's Dario Amodei urged the industry to slow capability improvements three days earlier, with Sam Altman and Elon Musk endorsing him within hours.

Zuckerberg said, "Any lab that doesn't focus on alignment will fall behind," adding that labs face significant liability if their models cause harm. He cited Meta's decision to delay the Muse agent release to strengthen security, noting the company did it without asking anyone else to go first. Meta has committed the significant majority of its compute to products serving immediate user needs rather than self-improving systems, and already uses independent evaluators, which he called industry best practice.

President Trump downplayed AI harm concerns on Monday, saying guardrails already exist and that doubt cast on development benefits China. FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson said Tuesday that everyone should be deeply suspicious of AI companies seeking antitrust exemptions while lobbying for regulation. Amodei had requested antitrust permission last week to let rivals coordinate a slower pace.

title: Zuckerberg Says Labs Don't Need Permission to Slow Down
